finalText:
Migration finished. 12 files converted, 36 call sites:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `repo/session.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js` |

Each `db.query(sql, params)` became `db.execute({ sql, params })`, matching the formatting of files migrated in earlier passes byte-for-byte (verified `repo/sla.js` against its already-migrated sibling `repo/macro.js`). All 77 files under `packages/` and `lib/` pass `node --check`.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

**`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** still calls `db.query`. Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on every upgrade with local changes silently lost — so patching it would be reverted and, worse, would hide the problem. This is the one real blocker to deleting `db.query` from `lib/db.js:13`: the deprecated method must stay until the vendored dep is upgraded to a version that calls `execute`, or you shim `query` at the adapter's `require` boundary. Worth an upstream ticket rather than an edit here.

**`cache.query(...)`** in ~20 repo files is untouched — that's the cache handle (`lib/cache.js`), a different API, not part of this migration.
